rows.label: Range
rows.value: 1 MHz–6 GHz; half-duplex transmit or receive.

rows.label: Samples
rows.value: 2–20 MS/s; 8-bit I and 8-bit Q.

rows.label: RF input maximum
rows.value: −5 dBm; exceeding this can permanently damage the receiver.

rows.label: Attenuation
rows.value: Use external attenuation for stronger signals; disabling the RX amplifier is not reliable protection.

rows.label: Transmit power
rows.value: Frequency-dependent; no single output-power value covers the whole tuning range.

rows.label: RF controls
rows.value: Software-controlled RX/TX gain and baseband filtering.

rows.label: Low sample rates
rows.value: Documentation recommends ≥8 MS/s acquisition, then filtered decimation for narrower streams.

rows.label: Antenna port
rows.value: 50 Ω SMA female.

rows.label: Connector fit
rows.value: SMA and RP-SMA may screw together without a working center contact.

rows.label: Antenna power
rows.value: Switchable 3.0–3.3 V, 50 mA maximum.

rows.label: Clock ports
rows.value: 10 MHz, 3.3 V square wave; CLKIN must remain between 0 and 3.3 V.

rows.label: Host power
rows.value: Supply 5 V at 500 mA through USB.

rows.label: USB port
rows.value: Micro-B connector with high-speed USB data.

rows.label: Included
rows.value: Enclosed HackRF One and micro-USB cable; antenna is separate.

rows.label: Expansion
rows.value: Internal headers and programming buttons; custom standalone operation requires appropriate firmware.

rows.label: Host throughput
rows.value: High-speed USB and sufficient CPU; shared USB traffic can restrict higher sample rates.

rows.label: Install
rows.value: libhackrf and HackRF Tools; official guide covers Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and Windows.

rows.label: Windows path
rows.value: Official guide points to radioconda binaries.

rows.label: Version matching
rows.value: Firmware may need updating to match host tools.

rows.label: Firmware image
rows.value: Use hackrf_one_usb.bin for SPI flash; model-specific .dfu is for recovery.

rows.label: Revision identification
rows.value: PCB silkscreen identifies revision; r6 onward also reports it through hackrf_info.

rows.label: Revision differences
rows.value: r9 changed RF/clock components; r10 largely returned to r8 design. Maker states common factory performance specifications.

rows.label: Design and downloads
rows.value: Firmware releases, host source and hardware designs are published by Great Scott Gadgets.

resources.label: One RF specifications and input limit

gaps: Clone boards and PortaPack bundles require their own revision and accessory checks; this profile describes Great Scott Gadgets HackRF One.
notes: Documentation reviewed; no RF measurements or firmware installation performed.

rows.label: Operating range
rows.value: 100 kHz–6 GHz; half-duplex transmit or receive.

rows.label: Tuning boundary
rows.value: Tunes 0 Hz–7.1 GHz; the wider tuning span is not its rated operating range.

rows.label: Standard samples
rows.value: 8-bit I/Q at up to 20 MS/s.

rows.label: Half-precision mode
rows.value: 4-bit I/Q at up to 40 MS/s; trades precision for throughput.

rows.label: Extended precision
rows.value: 16-bit I/Q; ≥16× decimation/interpolation; typical effective resolution 9–11 bits.

rows.label: FPGA
rows.value: Lattice iCE40UP5K; gateware is bundled with firmware.

rows.label: DC-offset removal
rows.value: FPGA signal paths offer an optional DC blocker.

rows.label: RF controls
rows.value: Software-set gain/filter; switchable RF-port supply: 3.3 V, 50 mA.

rows.label: USB
rows.value: USB-C connector with high-speed USB 2.0 data; USB-powered.

rows.label: Host supply
rows.value: Shared HackRF host guide specifies 5 V, 500 mA and high-speed USB.

rows.label: RF connector
rows.value: SMA; an RP-SMA antenna needs an adapter.

rows.label: Clock and trigger
rows.value: P1/P2 default to CLKIN/CLKOUT; default clock interface is 10 MHz, 0–3.3 V.

rows.label: Timing and shielding
rows.value: TCXO, installed RF shielding and a hardware transmit-disable facility.

rows.label: Package
rows.value: Plastic enclosure included; USB-C data cable and antenna are separate.

rows.label: Add-ons
rows.value: Maker names Opera Cake, most PortaPacks and some enclosures; verify the exact accessory.

rows.label: Existing applications
rows.value: Designed to run HackRF One applications by default; new modes need application support.

rows.label: Install
rows.value: Official libhackrf/HackRF Tools guide provides Linux, macOS, FreeBSD and Windows paths.

rows.label: Firmware image
rows.value: Use hackrf_pro_usb.bin; HackRF One uses a different image.

rows.label: Recovery
rows.value: Use the model-specific .dfu image for DFU recovery, then the .bin image for flash.

rows.label: Reviewed release
rows.value: 2026.01.3 release notes include a mixer-lock fix and access to Pro’s larger flash.

rows.label: Initial revision
rows.value: Official revision list identifies r1.2.1 as the first production Pro.

rows.label: Design files
rows.value: Dedicated Pro repository publishes KiCad hardware files; software lives in the shared HackRF repository.

gaps: A Pro-specific maximum RF-input power was not found in the reviewed official pages; HackRF One’s −5 dBm limit is not asserted for Pro.
Availability of each new FPGA mode in a particular application/release remains untested.
The product page still promises a forthcoming migration guide; do not promise a completed migration workflow.
notes: The product page’s broad DC-spike claim is narrowed to the optional DC blocker documented in the gateware reference.

rows.label: Model
rows.value: R828D tuner and 8-bit RTL2832U ADC; receive only.

rows.label: Capture bandwidth
rows.value: 2.56 MHz stable; 3.2 MHz may drop samples.

rows.label: HF path
rows.value: Built-in 28.8 MHz upconverter; compatible drivers handle the offset.

rows.label: Front end
rows.value: HF/VHF/UHF triplexer with automatic broadcast-band notch filtering.

rows.label: Filtering trade-off
rows.value: Launch measurements show reduced sensitivity on some bands; filters do not prevent all overload.

rows.label: Reference
rows.value: 1 ppm TCXO.

rows.label: RF port
rows.value: SMA input, typically 50 Ω.

rows.label: USB
rows.value: USB-A male; typical draw 250–270 mA.

rows.label: Bias tee
rows.value: Software-switched 4.5 V, up to 180 mA.

rows.label: Bias-tee load
rows.value: Do not enable into a directly connected DC-short antenna; follow the maker’s bias-tee wiring guide.

rows.label: Cooling
rows.value: Aluminium enclosure and thermal pad dissipate heat.

rows.label: Package choice
rows.value: V4 launched as dongle-only or antenna-set packages; confirm the exact seller bundle.

rows.label: Required drivers
rows.value: Use a V4-aware library; older applications may need their RTL-SDR DLL replaced.

rows.label: Windows driver
rows.value: Quickstart installs WinUSB for the RTL interface, normally Bulk-In Interface 0; verify USB ID 0BDA:2838:00.

rows.label: Application selection
rows.value: Select RTL-SDR USB as the SDR# source after driver setup.

rows.label: Linux and macOS
rows.value: V4 guide covers current librtlsdr installation; packaged old drivers can lack V4 support.

rows.label: Android
rows.value: Maker documents V4 support through updated SDR Driver and supported SDR applications.

rows.label: HF settings
rows.value: Use the upconverter path; V3 direct-sampling setup is not the V4 workflow.

rows.label: V4L is different
rows.value: V4L uses R828S and a diplexed front end; its software-support requirements differ.

rows.label: Stock boundary
rows.value: The 2023 launch page’s production forecast is historical, not a current V4 stock guarantee.

gaps: The reviewed V4 documents do not specify an absolute maximum RF-input power.
V4 listing availability and the precise antenna/cable contents need checking at purchase; V4L is a separate design.
notes: This profile remains for the R828D V4. V4L support or hardware specifications are not substituted.

rows.label: Native coverage
rows.value: 24–1700 MHz receive; HF needs an optional SpyVerter.

rows.label: Tuner
rows.value: R820T2 or R860 low-IF front end.

rows.label: ADC
rows.value: 12-bit, 20 MS/s; maker figures: 10.4 ENOB, 70 dB SNR, 95 dB SFDR.

rows.label: I/Q output
rows.value: 10 MS/s; 10 MHz view, up to 9 MHz alias/image-free.

rows.label: Reduced-rate mode
rows.value: 2.5 MS/s is experimental; use 10 MS/s plus decimation for dependable narrowband workflows.

rows.label: RF input maximum
rows.value: +10 dBm.

rows.label: Noise and linearity
rows.value: Maker figures: 3.5 dB NF at 42–1002 MHz; 35 dBm IIP3.

rows.label: Output format
rows.value: I/Q or real; 16-bit integer or 32-bit float.

rows.label: Processor
rows.value: Cortex-M4F up to 204 MHz with dual M0 cores.

rows.label: RF connectors
rows.value: SMA input; U.FL RF loopthrough.

rows.label: Bias tee
rows.value: Switchable 4.5 V; 50 mA budget.

rows.label: Clock
rows.value: 0.5 ppm reference, timestamp RTC; external 10–100 MHz reference through MCX.

rows.label: Expansion
rows.value: 16 SGPIO, eight GPIO, two ADC inputs, clock outputs and JTAG; see maker port diagram.

rows.label: HF accessory
rows.value: Connect SpyVerter IF output to R2 RF input; compatible software can power it through the bias tee.

rows.label: Temperature
rows.value: −10 to 40 °C; maintain ventilation.

rows.label: Suggested computer
rows.value: Third-generation Core i3 2.4 GHz equivalent, 2 GB RAM, high-speed USB 2.0.

rows.label: Host throughput
rows.value: Quickstart warns of dropped samples on slow hosts and discourages hubs at full rate.

rows.label: Platforms
rows.value: Maker lists Windows 10/11, Linux, BSD and macOS; application support varies.

rows.label: Windows setup
rows.value: Normally automatic; maker provides a WinUSB compatibility driver if detection fails.

rows.label: Linux/macOS API
rows.value: Open-source libairspy and host utilities are in airspyone_host.

rows.label: Firmware
rows.value: The Airspy One repository links build and flashing instructions in its wiki.

rows.label: Network receiver
rows.value: SPY Server has Windows and Linux builds; Linux x86-64 build requires AVX2 and FMA.

rows.label: ARM server choice
rows.value: Separate ARM64 and ARMHF downloads; select the host architecture.

rows.label: Plugin boundary
rows.value: The download page cautions that older plugins may fail with SDR# x64.

rows.label: Buffered I/O
rows.value: Eight tri-state pins; stated operating range 1.65–5 V.

rows.label: Pin tools
rows.value: Voltage measurement per pin and switchable 10 kΩ pull-ups.

rows.label: Connectors
rows.value: 10-pin 2.54 mm main header; 9-pin 1 mm auxiliary header.

rows.value: 1 Gbit (128 MB) NAND exposed as USB storage for settings/files.

rows.label: Status display
rows.value: 320 × 240 IPS; pin labels, voltages and supply current.

rows.label: Controls
rows.value: One button and 18 RGB LEDs.

rows.label: USB
rows.value: USB-C; data speed is limited by RP2040 hardware.

rows.label: Target supply
rows.value: 1–5 V output; rated maximum 300 mA.

rows.label: Protection setting
rows.value: 0–500 mA current-limit range; extra headroom is for transients, not a 500 mA output rating.

rows.value: Disabled in HiZ mode; current-limit trips shut the supply off.

rows.value: Pin 1: VOUT/VREF; pins 2–9: IO0–IO7; pin 10: target ground.

rows.label: Accessory requirement
rows.value: Probe and auxiliary cable kits are separate listed products; verify the purchased bundle.

rows.label: Firmware-controlled pins
rows.value: Protocol functions vary by mode; use the displayed pin labels and official pin map.

rows.label: Terminal
rows.value: Use a serial terminal; quickstart specifies 115200 baud, 8-N-1 and VT100.

rows.label: Two serial ports
rows.value: One is the terminal and one is binary access; numbering is not guaranteed.

rows.label: Platforms
rows.value: Official quickstart provides Windows, Linux and macOS terminal paths.

rows.label: Protocol reference
rows.value: SPI, I²C, UART and other modes have separate commands and limits.

rows.value: Production rev10 uses bus_pirate5_rev10.uf2; rev8 engineering samples use their own image.

rows.label: Design files
rows.value: Rev10 hardware documentation links schematics, component placement and an interactive BOM.

rows.label: Firmware channel
rows.value: Official downloads are automated builds from main; review the build and revision before updating.

gaps: The reviewed pages do not establish an absolute maximum input voltage for every external pin; 1.65–5 V is the stated buffered operating range.
Probe kit contents depend on the order; no host-terminal or accessory bundle is implied.

rows.value: 100 MS/s: ≤3 channels; 50: ≤6; 40: ≤7; 25: all eight.

rows.label: Analog rates

rows.value: 10-bit ADC; 1 MHz bandwidth at 10 MS/s.

rows.value: 0–5 V; readings saturate outside it.

rows.value: 1 MΩ parallel with 10 pF.

rows.label: Mixed capture
rows.value: Available rates depend on enabled digital/analog channels and USB bandwidth.

rows.value: ±25 V protection is distinct from the 0–5 V analog measuring range.

rows.label: USB
rows.value: High-speed USB 2.0; Logic Pro USB 3 requirements are separate.

rows.label: Supported OS

rows.value: Windows installer includes the hardware driver; macOS app and Linux AppImage have separate instructions.

rows.label: Capture duration
rows.value: Host memory, signal activity and settings limit recording length.

rows.value: Protocol decoders, triggers, measurements; CSV, binary, VCD and MATLAB export.

rows.value: Automation API and custom decoder support; use Logic 2 documentation.

rows.value: Logic 8 is distinct from first-generation Logic, Logic Pro 8 and Logic Pro 16.
